8.0.s.en: (3) Summary of chapters six and seven

8.0.0.en: Moses prepared everything according to the command of God, who chose Aaron and his sons for the priesthood. And all the people were present before the tabernacle to rejoice in the ordination of their priests.

8.0.1.en: Moses was a priest, or the middle stage between the head of the family being its priest and the setting apart of the priesthood in particular persons for the whole people, namely Aaron and his sons. God declared this in the Psalm: "Moses and Aaron among his priests" (Ps 99:6). Moses brought Aaron and his sons and all the people to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation for their ordination to take place there, for the following reasons:

8.0.2.en: 1- So that the people may know that their ordination is from God and by His command, and not a private idea of Moses out of love for his brother Aaron.

8.0.3.en: 2- So that the people may feel the majesty of the priesthood and respect it and submit to it.

8.0.4.en: 3- So that Aaron and his sons may feel their responsibility for the care of all the people of God gathered in their multitudes during the ordination.

8.0.5.en: Moses brought the requirements of the ordination, which are:

8.0.6.en: 1- The garments of the priesthood that Aaron and his sons would wear, mentioned in (Ex 28, 39).

8.0.7.en: 2- The anointing oil that Moses prepared, mentioned in (Ex 30:22-33).

8.0.8.en: 3- The animals to be slaughtered, which are a bull and two rams; the explanation of the ritual of offering them will come in this chapter (Ex 29).

8.0.9.en: 4- A basket with unleavened bread in it; the explanation of the ritual of offering it will come in this chapter (Ex 29).

8.1.0.en: The faithfulness of Moses was manifested in his conveying precisely what God says to the people.

8.2.1.en: The washing of the priests is a reference to the two sacraments of Baptism and Confession, which wash a person from his sins, for before the servant calls people to repentance he must first repent himself. The washing is a cleansing of the body from the outside in preparation for a great matter, the ordination to the priesthood, and it signifies purity of heart so that Aaron and his sons may serve God without any personal ends and shepherd His people in purity.

8.2.2.en: This ritual continues in the New Testament, for the priest washes his hands during the Liturgy for the same purposes mentioned before.

8.2.3.en: Moses completed the washing of Aaron and his sons in a special place of the tabernacle of the congregation, because it was a washing of the whole body, and not in the laver in which they would afterward wash their hands and feet before entering the sanctuary.

8.3.0.en: Moses brought the priestly garments that are mentioned in detail in (Ex 28) and put them on Aaron and his sons, and these garments point to the attributes and work of Christ as mentioned in the commentary on the Book of Exodus (Ex 28). These garments signify:

8.3.1.en: 1- The greatness of God and the dignity of serving Him.

8.3.2.en: 2- The importance of adorning ourselves with virtues to be children of God.

8.3.3.en: 3- The importance of purifying the heart and being clothed with righteousness when we stand before God.

8.3.4.en: 4- The splendor and majesty of the priesthood.

8.3.5.en: 5- These garments signify the garments of light that the children of God wear in the Kingdom (Rev 4:4).

8.4.0.en: Then he anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it and the priests themselves with the anointing oil, as a reference to the sanctification of the servants by the Holy Spirit, just as He descended on Christ in the waters of the Jordan to begin His ministry (Mt 3) and on the Church on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2). Thus the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation and likewise the priests became set apart for the service of God and not for any other work.

8.4.1.en: And the sprinkling of the oil seven times on the bronze altar signifies the perfection of sanctification, and it is done by sprinkling the oil with the finger seven times.

8.4.2.en: And the pouring of the oil on the head of Aaron, so that it ran down upon his beard and his garments, unlike the anointing of the priests on their foreheads with this oil, is because of the greatness of the responsibility of the high priest, who is responsible for the care of the priests and all the people.

8.5.0.en: After Moses had clothed Aaron with his garments and anointed him, he clothed the priests with their garments, mentioned in detail with all their meanings in (Ex 28).

8.5.1.en: The angels stand with reverence and purity and concentration of mind before God, praising Him at all times; so also should the priests and servants be during their service. So when you stand to pray or offer the service of God, humble yourself and fix your gaze on Christ and set aside all your concerns to enjoy being in His presence.

8.5.2.en: (2) The sacrifices offered for the priests (vv. 14-32:) 14 And he brought the bullock for the sin offering: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the bullock for the sin offering. 15 And he slew it; and Moses took the blood, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about with his finger, and purified the altar, and poured the blood at the bottom of the altar, and sanctified it, to make reconciliation upon it. 16 And he took all the fat that was upon the inwards, and the caul above the liver, and the two kidneys, and their fat, and Moses burned it upon the altar. 17 But the bullock, and his hide, his flesh, and his dung, he burnt with fire without the camp; as the LORD commanded Moses. 18 And he brought the ram for the burnt offering: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the ram. 19 And he killed it; and Moses sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about. 20 And he cut the ram into pieces; and Moses burnt the head, and the pieces, and the fat. 21 And he washed the inwards and the legs in water; and Moses burnt the whole ram upon the altar: it was a burnt sacrifice for a sweet savour, and an offering made by fire unto the LORD; as the LORD commanded Moses. 22 And he brought the other ram, the ram of consecration: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the ram. 23 And he slew it; and Moses took of the blood of it, and put it upon the tip of Aaron's right ear, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot. 24 And he brought Aaron's sons, and Moses put of the blood upon the tip of their right ear, and upon the thumbs of their right hands, and upon the great toes of their right feet: and Moses sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about. 25 And he took the fat, and the rump, and all the fat that was upon the inwards, and the caul above the liver, and the two kidneys, and their fat, and the right shoulder: 26 And out of the basket of unleavened bread, that was before the LORD, he took one unleavened cake, and a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, and put them on the fat, and upon the right shoulder: 27 And he put all upon Aaron's hands, and upon his sons' hands, and waved them for a wave offering before the LORD. 28 And Moses took them from off their hands, and burnt them on the altar upon the burnt offering: they were consecrations for a sweet savour: it is an offering made by fire unto the LORD. 29 And Moses took the breast, and waved it for a wave offering before the LORD: for of the ram of consecration it was Moses' part; as the LORD commanded Moses. 30 And Moses took of the anointing oil, and of the blood which was upon the altar, and sprinkled it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon his sons' garments with him; and sanctified Aaron, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons' garments with him. 31 And Moses said unto Aaron and to his sons, Boil the flesh at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and there eat it with the bread that is in the basket of consecrations, as I commanded, saying, Aaron and his sons shall eat it. 32 And that which remaineth of the flesh and of the bread shall ye burn with fire.

8.6.0.en: Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the bull, confessing their sins, so that this bull may bear their sins for them, and it is a symbol of the blood of Christ, which cleanses everyone who believes in Him, for it is necessary for the salvation of all, whether the common people or the priests. Then the bull is slaughtered and Moses smears the blood on the horns of the bronze altar and pours out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. We notice here that the one who performs the priestly work is Moses, and they do not enter with the blood into the sanctuary, because the priests have not yet been ordained.

8.6.1.en: Then Moses burns the fat on the altar, while the skin of the animal and the rest of its flesh and its waste are burned outside the camp and no one eats of them, because it is a sin offering for the priests, as passed in (ch. 4).

8.7.0.en: Then he offered the burnt offering for them, a ram, according to the ritual explained before in (Ex 29:

8.7.1.en: 15-18), to show that Christ, who died on the Cross in obedience to the Father, fully satisfied divine justice, so that God was pleased with humanity in Christ. By this Aaron and his sons declare their readiness to please God and to offer their whole lives to His service.

8.8.0.en: The third offering and sacrifice was the second ram, which is the ram of "consecration," and consecration means the filling of the hand, and the spiritual purpose of it is that the servants should not come forward to the service of God with empty hands and life, but full of the fruits of the Spirit.

8.8.1.en: What is meant by the sacrifice of consecration is the beginning of the priest's service, that is, the sharing of Aaron and his sons in offering the sacrifice to God. It resembles to some extent the peace offering, with some differences that will appear in the explanation of the following verses.

8.9.0.en: The tip of the ear: the lower part of the outer ear.

8.9.1.en: Thumb, great toe: the big finger of the hand or foot.

8.9.2.en: After Moses slaughters the ram of consecration, he anoints the ear and the thumb and the great toe of the right hand and foot of Aaron and his sons, and this signifies the opening of the ear to hear and understand the word of God, and the sanctification of the hand for doing His pleasure, and the readiness of the feet to walk in His way. Then the blood of the sacrifice is poured out and the fat burned, as explained before in (Ex 29:19, 20).

8.10.0.en: He offered to the Lord an unleavened cake and a cake of bread and a wafer, after waving them before the Lord, as a declaration that He is the source of all grace by His pure life like the unleavened, and satisfying like the bread, and gentle like the wafer, as explained before in (Ex 29:23-25). And Moses put this unleavened bread and wafer with the fat and the right shoulder on the hands of the priests and waved them before God and then burned them on the altar.

8.11.0.en: Then he waved the breast and took it as a portion for himself as the servant of the sacrifice, as explained before in (Ex 29:26).

8.12.0.en: Moses sanctified Aaron and his sons and their garments with the anointing oil and the blood of the sacrifice, in a clear reference to the work of the Holy Spirit (the anointing oil) and the blood of Christ for the sanctification of man. And he gave them their portion to eat on the same day and to burn what is left over (Ex 29:21, 31-34).

8.12.1.en: Before you speak to people about God or advise them about anything, take care of your personal relationship with Him in repentance and prayers and reading in the Holy Bible, so that you are strengthened by the grace of God and your words are effective with those who hear you.

8.13.s.en: (3) The duration of the completion of the consecration of the priests

8.13.0.en: The days of your consecration: the days of your ordination and consecration.

8.13.1.en: The Lord has commanded to do: that is, the ritual of the first day is repeated for the seven days.

8.13.2.en: The ritual of ordination extends to the completion of seven days, as a pledge that the consecrated servant will spend his whole life, the period of his sojourn on earth, in the service of God without turning back. And God promises him that He will supply his need and fill his hand with provision and good all the days of his life. In the New Testament the priest spends forty days after his ordination in retreat and worship in preparation for service throughout his life.

8.13.3.en: And Aaron and his sons remain inside the house of the Lord these seven days, taking care not to enter the sanctuary because their ordination has not been completed. The rituals of ordination that took place on the first day, of washing and offering the sacrifices and the food, are repeated each day of the seven days.

8.14.0.en: God warns the priests through Moses not to go out from the house of the Lord for seven days lest they be punished with death, and this is as a symbol of the consecration of their lives to God, so that they do not do the works of the world, otherwise they become as dead in the sight of God. In these seven days they complete the worship of God and the rituals of ordination.

8.15.0.en: Aaron and his sons obeyed and carried out everything that God commanded.

8.15.1.en: Our consecration to Christ by Baptism and the Holy Myron has made us His servants throughout the whole of our lives. We serve Him with all our energies and He is responsible for us and for all our needs; this is our way as Christians in our lives.

9.0.s.en: (1) Sacrifices for the priests and the people

9.0.0.en: Moses brought Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel on the eighth day of their ordination. It signifies eternal life after the present time with its seven days, and the eighth day is the beginning of their service after the completion of their consecration. And he called the elders as representatives of the people.

9.1.0.en: Moses no longer offered the sacrifices after the consecration of Aaron and his sons, and the priests began to offer from their own means for themselves a sin offering as an expression of their personal repentance and their confession of their error and their need of the cleansing blood of Christ, and then a burnt offering as an expression of the consecration of their lives, so that their obedience to God becomes complete (ch. 4, 1). The scholars of the Jews think that this sin offering was an atonement for the sin of making the golden calf. In general, the repetition of offering sin offerings, since they offered a sin offering during their ordination, expresses:

9.1.1.en: 1- That the sacrifice of blood does not give complete forgiveness, whereas the sacrifice of Christ gives complete forgiveness.

9.1.2.en: 2- Their constant need as human beings for the forgiveness of their sins, which occur throughout their lives.

9.2.0.en: After the priests offered sacrifices for themselves, they offered sacrifices and offerings for the people, that they too might be cleansed, because they had shared in the worship of the golden calf in addition to the rest of their sins.. The following is noticed in the sacrifices and offerings:

9.2.1.en: 1- They begin with a sin offering, which is a kid of the goats, because it is not possible to stand before God except after getting rid of sin.

9.2.2.en: 2- Then the offering of a burnt offering, which is a calf and a lamb of the first year, that is, each of them a year old, which signifies maturity and at the same time innocence, and it means the consecration of the heart to God, as the sacrifice is burned entirely on the altar.

9.2.3.en: 3- After getting rid of sin and declaring the consecration of the heart to God, fellowship with Him is possible, so they offer a peace offering, which is a bullock and a ram.

9.2.4.en: 4- In the end they offer offerings which are fine flour mingled with oil, as a declaration of offering all their possessions to God and of their seeking His blessing in their lives.

9.2.5.en: With this preparation they are able to meet God and enjoy the sight of Him.

9.3.0.en: Moses and the priests took the sacrifices and offerings to the front of the tabernacle of the congregation and went in with them before the bronze altar, and with them were the representatives of the people, that is, the elders, for the offering of the sacrifices and offerings. And Moses said to them that the offering of these sacrifices is the condition of preparation for meeting God.

9.4.0.en: The horns of the altar: that is, the altar of incense inside the sanctuary.

9.4.1.en: The bottom of the altar: that is, the bronze altar.

9.4.2.en: Aaron began by offering the first sacrifice, which is the sin offering for himself and for his sons the priests, and he slaughtered it at the side of the bronze altar on the north, and took some of the blood and anointed the horns of the altar and poured out the rest at the bottom of it.

9.5.0.en: Then he offered the fat of the sacrifice and burned it on the bronze altar, while the skin of the animal and all its flesh he burned outside the camp.

9.6.0.en: After that he offered the burnt offering and sprinkled its blood round about on the bronze altar, while the flesh of the sacrifice he cut into pieces and washed and burned all of it on the altar.

9.7.0.en: After the priests offered sacrifices for themselves, they offered for the people a sin offering, which was the kid, and they burned all of it outside the camp and did not eat of it this time, because of the death of the two sons of Aaron for their sin (ch. 10:1, 2, 16-20), since they sinned during the seven days of their ordination and died.

9.8.0.en: Then he offered the burnt offering for the people and likewise the grain offering, for he took his handful of it and offered it on the altar, all these sacrifices in addition to the morning burnt offering that was offered before all the sacrifices offered for the priests or for the people.

9.9.0.en: Then he offered the peace offerings for the people, which were the bullock and the ram, and after slaughtering them he offered their fat on the altar, while their breasts were eaten by the priests and the rest of the flesh was probably eaten by the elders of the people on its behalf.

9.9.1.en: Offer repentance for your sins before you require it of those around you; it is good to teach those around you, but be an example to them in examining yourself and offering prayers and worship, and you will save your own soul and those for whom you are responsible.

9.10.s.en: (2) The blessing and the holy fire

9.10.0.en: Came down: because the altar of burnt offering was three cubits high, about a meter and a half, and they would go up on it by a sloping surface, because the Law forbade the use of a ladder (Ex 20:26). The lifting of the hand to pronounce the ritual blessing (Num 6:22-26) represents the authority of the priesthood, and this blessing is completed after the offering of the sacrifice, because the blood of Christ is the foundation of every blessing. The Church has taken this, since at the end of every church service the priest raises his hand with the cross, giving the blessing of Christ to all the people before their departure.

9.11.0.en: The entering of Moses, the chief of the prophets, with Aaron, the high priest, into the tabernacle means the importance of the word of God on the tongue of the apostles and prophets in the Holy Bible, and the importance of the work of the priesthood and the ritual of the Church for our salvation.

9.11.1.en: Thus the second blessing was completed, and their entering together was for Moses to hand over the rituals of the service to Aaron. The appearing of the glory of the Lord was perhaps in the form of a cloud or fire or incense or other spiritual phenomena, and this signifies the presence of Christ in the Church.

9.11.2.en: It is noted that the steps that took place before the appearing of the glory of God and what follows it are:

9.11.3.en: 1- The offering of the sacrifices for the priests and the people.

9.11.5.en: 3- Aaron's coming down from the bronze altar (v. 22).

9.11.6.en: 4- The entering of Moses and Aaron into the sanctuary, perhaps so that Moses might explain and confirm to Aaron how to serve in the sanctuary (v. 23).

9.11.7.en: 5- Their coming out from the sanctuary and their blessing of the people a second time (v. 23).

9.11.8.en: 6- The appearing of the glory of the Lord, and this was the second time after its appearing at the completion of the setting up of the tabernacle (v. 23).

9.11.9.en: 7- The coming out of fire from before God and its burning of the sacrifices (v. 24).

9.11.10.en: 8- The people's bowing down and shouting (v. 24).

9.12.0.en: Fire came out from before the Lord and extended to the altar and burned the sacrifices, for the Holy Spirit by His fire burns our sins and cleanses us. The shouting of the people is a proof of their joy in the Lord, while their bowing down is reverence and worship of Him. The appearing of the fire and its burning of the sacrifices means:

9.12.1.en: 1- The greatness of God and His glory.

9.12.2.en: 2- God's satisfaction with His people and His acceptance of their sacrifices.

9.12.3.en: 3- God's confirmation of His covenant with His people by means of the sacrifices, which are a symbol of the sacrifice of Christ.

9.12.4.en: 4- His acceptance of the service of the priests.

9.12.5.en: Hold fast to your spiritual worship and trust that God wants to appear in your life in different forms to reassure you and gladden your heart, so that you advance in your spiritual life and hold fast to Him more and more.

9.12.6.en: The death of the two sons of Aaron. This chapter shows us the attributes required of the priests of the Old Testament, which signify the attributes of the priests and servants of the New Testament. These attributes are:

9.12.8.en: 3- Not being occupied with anything other than the service 4- Not drinking intoxicants, and discernment and discrimination
